limits: Cannot change governance decisions, contract configuration or deployed code.

trusted: Governance treats one debt token as worth one vault asset.
Contracts are deployed exactly as written, with the configuration in the source.
environment: The vault was deployed with the lending pair and holds no deposits and no shares before the attacker acts.
The lending pair holds 10,000,000 debt tokens ready to lend.
The vault's asset keeps its value; there is no external market price to manipulate.
excluded: Bugs in the vault asset or the debt token beyond the code shown.
Gas or denial-of-service griefing against these contracts.
threat_model.property: No sequence of transactions by this attacker borrows more debt tokens than its collateral redeems for, or leaves the lending pair with debt its collateral does not cover.

root_cause.detail: the oracle passes the vault's share price through with no bound, so a donation to the empty vault can push it above 1e36 and the pair's 1e36 / price exchange rate floors to zero

0-target.assumes: the oracle price stays small enough that 1e36 / price keeps its precision

1-upstream.assumes: the vault's share price is its true redemption value
1-upstream.guarantees: the price equals convertToAssets(1e18), with no bound

2-upstream.guarantees: shares redeem at their fair value, even after a donation

propagation_path: 2-upstream: a 2,000-token donation to the empty ShareVault followed by a 3-token deposit mints one wei of shares redeemable for about 2.001 tokens after accounting for the 1,000 virtual shares
0-target: LendingPair._updateExchangeRate computes 1e36 / price, which floors to zero
0-target: LendingPair._isSolvent computes a loan-to-value of zero, so borrow lends the pair's whole balance against one wei of shares
expected_reviewer_finding: The pair divides 1e36 by an unbounded vault share price; donating to the empty vault inflates that price past 1e36, the exchange rate floors to zero, and any borrow passes the solvency check.
simplifications: One vault, one oracle and one pair instead of the protocol's pair registry, interest and liquidation code
The donation goes to the vault's own balance; in the incident it went to the market controller that tracks the vault's assets
The debt token is held by the pair instead of minted on borrow, and no swap or flash-loan repayment is modelled
Amounts follow the incident's scale (a 2,000 donation, one wei of shares, 10,000,000 borrowed) but are illustrative

The fix bounds the oracle price, one of the two checks the protocol added; the other, a revert on a zero exchange rate in the pair, is left out so the versions differ in one file (https://github.com/resupplyfi/resupply)
